item.title: When the Same Taste Signal Leads to Opposite Choices — Chandrashekar's Dish Bitter Receptor Screen, Zhao & Mueller's RASSL Spiradoline Routing & Human TAS2R16 Expressed in Mouse Sweet vs. Bitter Cells
item.description: Labeled-line coding in mammalian taste: separating molecular ligand detection in heterologous cells (Chandrashekar et al. 2000; Bufe et al. 2002 TAS2R16) from behavioral attraction vs. aversion in mice when the exact same engineered receptor (spiradoline RASSL, Zhao 2003) or human bitter receptor (TAS2R16, Mueller 2005) is expressed in T1R2 sweet cells vs. T2R bitter cells.

item.title: How a Blood Test Tracks the Insulin Your Body Makes — Berson & Yalow's 1956–1960 Competitive 131I-Insulin Radioimmunoassay, Melani's 1970 Serum C-Peptide Separation & Modern Two-Antibody Electrochemiluminescence
item.description: How an unexpected antibody artifact became the foundation of clinical endocrinology: Berson & Yalow's (1956-1960) competitive radioimmunoassay (where rising unlabeled hormone lowers the bound-to-free tracer ratio), Melani, Rubenstein & Steiner's (1970) detection of equimolar co-secreted C-peptide in human serum, and modern two-antibody electrochemiluminescent C-peptide testing in insulin-treated patients.

item.title: How an Audiogram Finds Which Ear Heard the Tone — Fletcher & Wegel's 1922 Calibrated Thresholds, Transcranial Bone-Conduction Crossover, Denes & Naunton's Narrowband Noise & Hood's 1957 Masking Plateau
item.description: Acoustics and clinical logic of pure-tone audiometry and contralateral masking (H050): Fletcher & Wegel's (1922) calibrated receiver thresholds, skull-vibration crossover to the non-test cochlea, Denes & Naunton's (1952) frequency-band masking efficiency, and J.D. Hood's (1957) plateau method separating cross-heard responses from true ear-specific air- and bone-conduction thresholds.

item.title: The Protein That Met Resistance — Mouse 2×2 Dietary Amino Acid & Progressive Weight-Pulling Factorial (Trautman 2023), Sestrin2–Leucine Pocket & GATOR2 Cryo-EM vs. Longland & Layman Human Trials
item.description: Separating body-composition compartments, individual muscle hypertrophy, and glycemic tolerance when dietary protein meets resistance load: Trautman et al.'s (2023) 2x2 mouse amino-acid/weight-pulling factorial (protecting against fat accretion while leaving high-protein glucose intolerance unchanged, P=0.7442), Sestrin2–leucine and GATOR2 structural mechanics, Drummond's human rapamycin biopsy tracer study, and Longland (2016) vs. Layman (2005) human trials.

item.title: The Sugar That Stayed in the Scan — [18F]FDG from 1976–1979 Brain Autoradiography (Sokoloff & Reivich) and Cyclotron 109.77-Min Decay to GLUT3/Hexokinase II Trapping (4ZW9/2NZT), Thoracic SUVmax 7.2 & EBUS Granulomas
item.description: From cyclotron target to thoracic staging needle: Sokoloff's 1977 [14C]deoxyglucose method and Reivich/Alavi/Phelps's 1976-1979 human [18F]FDG brain studies, Hamacher nucleophilic synthesis and 109.77-minute half-life batch logistics (21 CFR 212.70), D-glucose-bound GLUT3 (PDB 4ZW9) and human hexokinase II (PDB 2NZT) metabolic trapping, 511-keV coincidence physics and SUVbw math (7.2 g/mL), and why bilateral FDG-avid mediastinal nodes still require EBUS-TBNA tissue confirmation (granulomatous inflammation vs. metastasis).

item.title: How a Blood Vessel Tells Itself to Relax — Furchgott & Zawadzki's 1980 Intact vs. Rubbed Rabbit Aorta, Rubanyi's Donor-Detector Perfusion, Palmer & Moncada's Ozone Chemiluminescence Nitric Oxide Proof & 15N-Arginine Tracing
item.description: How the vascular endothelium's relaxing signal was identified as nitric oxide: Furchgott & Zawadzki's (1980) discovery that removing the inner endothelial lining abolishes acetylcholine relaxation while preserving smooth-muscle contraction, Rubanyi et al.'s (1985) upstream donor/downstream denuded detector bioassay, Palmer, Ferrige & Moncada's (1987) chemiluminescent nitric oxide measurement alongside Ignarro's cGMP comparison, and 15N-arginine precursor tracing.

item.title: How a Sea Slug Gets Used to a Touch — Pinsker's Aplysia Gill-Withdrawal Habituation, Castellucci & Kandel's 1974 Quantal Failure Analysis & Bailey & Chen's Electron-Microscopy Presynaptic Active Zones
item.description: From behavioral habituation to synaptic quantal release and ultrastructure in Aplysia: Pinsker et al.'s (1970) gill-withdrawal habituation and dishabituation, Castellucci & Kandel's (1974) quantal variance/failure proof that short-term habituation reflects fewer transmitter packets released per impulse rather than smaller postsynaptic unit responses, and Bailey & Chen's (1983) electron microscopy of long-term habituated sensory-neuron varicosities.

item.title: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS
item.description: Two ward records seventy years apart: chlorpromazine's transition from Rhône-Poulenc synthesis (US2645640A) and Laborit's 1952 surgical 'artificial hibernation' to Delay & Deniker's psychiatric cases, Elkes & Elkes's 1954 crossover, and the 1964 NIMH Collaborative Study, paired with a contemporary pause-triggered torsades workup (Fridericia QTc 531 ms), ligand-free human hERG cryo-EM (PDB 5VA1), oocyte vs. CHO IC50s (21.6 vs. 1.47 µM), and DRD2 residence kinetics.

item.title: The Aspirin That Changed the Breathing — Hoffmann's Acetylsalicylic Acid, Vane's Prostaglandin Blockade & Human COX-2 Ser530 Acetylation (5F19 vs. 5F1A), Mitochondrial Uncoupling, Chloride Electrode Artifacts & EXTRIP Dialysis
item.description: Covalent enzyme acetylation meets clinical toxicology: Hoffmann's 1900 aspirin patent, Vane and Smith & Willis's 1971 prostaglandin inhibition, Roth's irreversible platelet COX acetylation, and Lucido's human COX-2 crystal structures (acetylated Ser530 in PDB 5F19 vs. salicylate-bound 5F1A), paired with a serial salicylate poisoning timeline showing mixed respiratory alkalosis and high-anion-gap acidosis, salicylate-induced chloride ISE pseudohyperchloremia, mitochondrial protonophoric uncoupling, pH-dependent nonionized CNS entry, and EXTRIP hemodialysis criteria.

item.title: How Scientists Found a Cycle in Cell Respiration — Krebs & Johnson's 1937 Pigeon-Breast Oxygen Flasks (342 to 1,385 µL), Malonate Succinate Trapping Under O2 vs. N2 & Stern-Ochoa Condensing Enzyme
item.description: How Krebs & Johnson (1937) proved cell respiration runs in a catalytic cycle rather than a linear chain: super-additive oxygen uptake with trace citrate in minced pigeon breast muscle, malonate blockade trapping succinate forward from citrate and oxaloacetate under oxygen, citrate resynthesis from oxaloacetate, and Stern, Ochoa & Lynen's (1951-1952) purified citrate synthase step.

item.title: How a Locust Turns Sound into Current — Michelsen's Abdominal Frequency Tuning, Windmill's Laser-Scanned Tympanum Waves, Warren's Auditory Receptor Currents & Chaiyasitdhi's 2-µm Axial Pull vs. Push
item.description: Biophysics of insect tympanal hearing in the desert locust: Michelsen's (1968) receptor frequency tuning, Windmill et al.'s (2008) laser-vibrometry frequency-sorting waves across the abdominal tympanum, Warren & Matheson's (2018) isolated transduction currents, and Chaiyasitdhi et al.'s (2025 reviewed preprint) direct 2-µm cap pull vs. push recordings.

item.title: How a Cell Opens Its Own Calcium Store — Streb, Irvine, Berridge & Schulz's 1983 Permeabilized Acinar IP3 Release, Ferris's Purified IP3 Receptor Lipid Vesicles & Callamaras's Confocal Puffs-to-Waves
item.description: How second-messenger calcium mobilization from internal stores was proven step by step: Streb, Irvine, Berridge & Schulz (1983) IP3-triggered Ca2+ release in permeabilized pancreatic acinar cells, Ferris et al. (1989) reconstitution of purified IP3 receptor into artificial lipid vesicles proving one protein both binds IP3 and forms the Ca2+ channel, and Callamaras et al. (1998) optical flash-photolysis puffs and waves.

item.title: How the End of a Pathway Slows the Beginning — Yates & Pardee's Pyrimidine Feedback, Gerhart & Schachman's Dissociated Catalytic vs. Regulatory ATCase Subunits & the 1965 MWC Allosteric Model
item.description: Birth of molecular allostery: from Yates & Pardee's (1956) pyrimidine end-product inhibition in E. coli to Gerhart & Pardee's (1962) heat-desensitized aspartate transcarbamoylase (ATCase), Gerhart & Schachman's (1965) separation and reassembly of catalytic and regulatory subunits, and the Monod-Wyman-Changeux (1965) conformational equilibrium model.

item.title: Why a Fly's Eye Went Quiet in the Light — Cosens & Manning's 1969 Drosophila trp Mutant, Montell's Gene Rescue, Hardie & Minke's Ca2+-Selective Current, Niemeyer's trp/trpl Double Mutant & Asp621 Pore Selectivity
item.description: Discovery of the founding TRP ion channel in Drosophila vision: Cosens & Manning's (1969) transient receptor potential mutant fading in continuous light, Montell & Rubin's gene rescue and cloning, Hardie & Minke's (1992) single-photoreceptor patch-clamp proof of missing Ca2+ permeability, Niemeyer et al.'s (1996) trp/trpl dissection, and Liu et al.'s (2007) pore-selectivity mutagenesis.

item.title: How a Cell Detects an Energy Shortfall — Carling & Hardie's Shared ACC/HMG-CoA Reductase Kinase (AMPK), Hawley's Thr172 & LKB1–STRAD–MO25 Complex, Sanders's PP2Cα Protection & Gowans's AMP vs. ADP Allostery
item.description: Dissecting the eukaryotic energy sensor AMPK: Carling, Zammit & Hardie's (1987) discovery that a single AMP-responsive kinase inhibits both fatty-acid and sterol synthesis, Hawley et al.'s identification of Thr172 phosphorylation by LKB1–STRAD–MO25, Sanders et al.'s (2007) cell-free proof that AMP binding shields Thr172 from dephosphorylation, and Gowans et al.'s (2013) separation of ADP/AMP protection from AMP allosteric catalysis.

item.title: The Iron Test Before the School Bell — Non-Anemic Adolescent Iron Deficiency (TSAT 9.5%, Ferritin 10 µg/L), Human Ferroportin–Hepcidin Cryo-EM (6WBV), Alternate-Day Isotope Absorption & Thai vs. Baltimore School Trials
item.description: Separating storage biomarkers from classroom endpoints in iron deficiency without anemia: assay reference intervals vs. WHO/2026 AAP ferritin thresholds, human ferroportin–hepcidin cryo-EM occlusion and Co2+/Fe2+-coupled binding (PDB 6WBV, Kd 210 -> 2.5 nM), Stoffel's erythrocyte stable-isotope absorption trial (16.3% daily vs. 21.8% alternate-day), and Sungthong's Thai school trial (n=397) vs. Bruner's Baltimore verbal-learning RCT (n=81).

item.title: Three Sodium Levels, Two Diets, One Blood Pressure — Controlled DASH-Sodium Feeding Trial (n=412, −8.9 mmHg Path), 24-Hour Urinary Excretion, Human NCC–Hydrochlorothiazide Cryo-EM (9BWT), Urinary Vesicles & GWAS Limits
item.description: Controlled feeding trials meet distal-tubule atomic physiology: Sacks et al.'s (2001) DASH-Sodium parallel-diet/crossover-salt design (n=412, why non-additive interaction yields -8.9 mmHg rather than -12.6 mmHg), energy-scaled sodium density vs. 24h urine potentiometry, human phosphorylated NCC and hydrochlorothiazide cryo-EM (PDB 9BWT), KCl urinary extracellular vesicle readouts, and UK Biobank/CHARGE MTHFS gene-diet slope limits.

item.title: Windows, Workloads, and Diffusing Gas — Ambulatory ECG Cadence & EMBRACE/CRYSTAL AF Trials (H041), Exercise Stress Physiology, HRR & ISCHEMIA (H042) & Plethysmographic Lung Volumes & DLCO/KCO (H043)
item.description: Clinical Cluster & Cardiopulmonary Physiology synthesis of ambulatory ECG monitoring (H041), cardiac exercise stress testing (H042), and lung volumes/DLCO (H043): Barrett's paired patch cohort (n=146), EMBRACE (n=572) & CRYSTAL AF (n=441), nocturnal vagal variants, and toothbrush pseudo-VT; coronary autoregulation, ST localization laws, LBBB vasodilator rule, Cole's HRR (n=2,428), WOMEN & ISCHEMIA; and Boyle's Law plethysmography vs. gas dilution, Roughton-Forster DLCO/KCO physics, CPFE/PAH phenotypes, ppo-DLCO, and race-neutral GLI Z-scores.

item.title: How Cells Tie Growth to Available Nutrients — Heitman & Hall's Yeast FPR1/TOR1/TOR2 Rapamycin Mutants, Sabatini & Brown's Mammalian mTOR Affinity Capture & Hara's Amino-Acid Withdrawal Gate
item.description: Discovery of the TOR nutrient-sensing pathway: Heitman, Movva & Hall (1991) genetic screen in Saccharomyces cerevisiae showing rapamycin requires FKBP12 (FPR1) to inhibit TOR1/TOR2, Sabatini et al. (1994) & Brown et al. (1994) biochemical capture of the ~289 kDa mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) only when rapamycin is bound to FKBP12, Barbet et al. (1996) starvation-like translation arrest, and Hara et al. (1998) amino-acid gating of insulin-stimulated p70S6K phosphorylation.

item.title: How Scientists Saw ATP Synthase Turn — Abrahams & Walker's Asymmetric F1 Crystal States, Noji & Yoshida's Spinning Actin Filament (120° Steps) & Itoh's Magnetic-Bead Mechanical ATP Synthesis
item.description: Direct proof of rotary catalysis in F1-ATPase: Abrahams et al. (1994) 2.8 Å crystal snapshot of three distinct catalytic β conformations around an asymmetric γ axle, Noji et al. (1997) single-molecule fluorescence microscopy of unidirectional counterclockwise γ rotation and Yasuda et al. (1998) discrete 120° steps, and Itoh et al. (2004) electromagnet-driven clockwise rotation forcing net ATP synthesis.

item.title: How a Cell Builds Insulin from One Chain — Sanger's Two-Chain Disulfide Puzzle, Steiner & Oyer's 1967 Human Islet Tumor Pulse-Chase Proinsulin Precursor & Equimolar C-Peptide Secretion
item.description: Discovery of prohormone processing: why isolated insulin A and B chains recombine inefficiently in vitro, Steiner & Oyer (1967) identification of single-chain proinsulin in human islet-cell adenoma slices, pulse-chase proof of intracellular proteolytic conversion into two-chain insulin, and Rubenstein, Clark & Steiner (1969) equimolar C-peptide co-secretion enabling clinical distinction between endogenous and exogenous insulin.

item.title: How a Cell Passes a Message Inside — Sutherland & Rall's Broken-Cell Liver Homogenate Fractionation, Heat-Stable Cyclic AMP Transfer & Walsh's cAMP-Dependent Protein Kinase
item.description: Discovery of the second-messenger principle: Rall, Sutherland & Berthet (1957) two-stage cell-free assay separating particulate membrane hormone response from soluble phosphorylase activation via a dialyzable, heat-stable factor, Sutherland & Rall (1958) chemical identification of cyclic 3',5'-AMP, and Walsh, Perkins & Krebs (1968) discovery of cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA).

item.title: How a Cell Senses Low Oxygen — Semenza's EPO 3' Enhancer & HIF-1α/β Purification, Maxwell's VHL Ubiquitin-Tagged Normoxic Degradation & Ivan/Jaakkola's Pro564 Oxygen-Dependent Hydroxylation
item.description: Molecular mechanism of cellular oxygen sensing: Semenza et al. (1991) & Wang et al. (1995) identification of the hypoxia-response element and HIF-1α/ARNT heterodimer, Maxwell et al. (1999) proof that pVHL targets HIF-α for oxygen-dependent ubiquitylation and proteasomal destruction, and Ivan et al. (2001) & Jaakkola et al. (2001) discovery of enzymatic Pro564 4-hydroxylation as the direct oxygen switch.

item.title: How a Cell Pumps Ions Uphill — Skou's 1957 Crab-Nerve Na++K+-Synergistic ATPase, Post's Phosphoenzyme Intermediate, Garrahan & Glynn's 3 Na+:2 K+:1 ATP Stoichiometry & Goldin's Inside-Out Vesicles
item.description: Enzymology and vectorial reconstitution of the sodium-potassium pump: Skou (1957) discovery of the Mg2+/Na+/K+-activated ATPase in Carcinus maenas nerve membranes, Post, Sen & Rosenthal (1965) acyl-phosphate intermediate formed with Na+ and hydrolyzed with K+, Garrahan & Glynn (1967) 3 Na+ : 2 K+ : 1 ATP coupling ratio in resealed red-cell ghosts, and Goldin (1977) inside-out liposome reconstitution.

item.title: The Gluten Fragment That Changed Its Charge — Celiac TG2 Cys277 Gln→Glu Deamidation, HLA-DQ2.5 Lysβ71 Pocket (1S9V), Irreversible ZED1227 Active-Site Trapping & Gluten-Challenge Biopsy Trials
item.description: Atomic pathogenesis and covalent enzyme inhibition in celiac disease: tissue transglutaminase 2 (TG2) Cys277 thioester deamidation of gliadin glutamine into negatively charged glutamate, HLA-DQ2.5 positively charged P4/P6/P7 pocket anchoring via Lysβ71 (PDB 1S9V), tTG-IgA vs. total IgA and Marsh/villus-height-to-crypt-depth morphometry, and Schuppan et al.'s (2021) NEJM ZED1227 trial.

item.title: How Scientists Recorded a Single Ion Channel — Katz & Miledi's Acetylcholine Noise Variance, Neher & Sakmann's 1976 Frog Muscle Pipette Steps & Hamill's Gigaseal Configurations
item.description: From statistical fluctuation analysis to direct single-molecule electrophysiology: Katz & Miledi (1972) inferring elementary acetylcholine events from voltage noise, Neher & Sakmann (1976) resolving discrete ~2.2 pA square current steps across a micro-patch of denervated frog muscle, and Hamill et al. (1981) gigaohm glass-membrane seals enabling cell-attached, whole-cell, inside-out, and outside-out configurations.

item.title: How a Potassium Channel Chooses an Ion — Bezanilla & Armstrong's Squid Axon Na+ Block, Heginbotham's TVGYG Signature Mutations & Doyle & MacKinnon's KcsA Selectivity Filter
item.description: Atomic solution to the potassium channel selectivity paradox: Bezanilla & Armstrong (1972) >10:1 K+/Na+ selectivity and internal Na+ block in perfused squid axons, Heginbotham et al. (1994) TVGYG pore-loop mutagenesis converting a K+-selective pore into a nonselective cation channel, Doyle et al. (1998) & Zhou et al. (2001) 2.0 Å KcsA crystal structures showing backbone carbonyl cages matching dehydrated K+, and Thompson et al. (2009) planar Na+ binding.

item.title: How Scientists Followed Carbon Through a Tumor — Warburg's 1927 Artery-Vein Lactate Balance, DeBerardinis's 13C NMR Glioblastoma TCA & Glutaminolysis & Hensley's Intraoperative Lung Tumor Infusions
item.description: From the classical Warburg Effect to human intraoperative stable-isotope tracing: Warburg, Wind & Negelein (1927) aerobic glycolysis across rat tumor vessels, DeBerardinis et al. (2007) 13C NMR isotopomer resolution of simultaneous glycolysis, TCA flux, fatty acid synthesis, and glutamine anaplerosis in glioblastoma cells, and Hensley et al. (2016) intraoperative [U-13C]glucose infusions in human NSCLC patients.

item.title: The Fat That Never Got Digested — Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency, Fecal Elastase CELA3A/3B ELISA vs. 72-Hour Fat Balance, Lipase-Colipase Lid Opening (1LPB) & Enteric Pancrelipase Trials
item.description: From watery-stool dilution artifacts in fecal elastase testing and Tóth's discovery that 'elastase-1' monoclonals actually measure CELA3B/CELA3A to 72-hour coefficient of fat absorption (CFA) balance math, Egloff's human pancreatic lipase-colipase open-lid crystal structure (PDB 1LPB), enteric-coated pancrelipase pH release kinetics, Whitcomb's 54-patient randomized trial, and fibrosing colonopathy incidence.

item.title: When the Same Sound Becomes a Surprise — Sutton's P300 Uncertainty Cue, Bekinschtein's Local-vs.-Global Oddball Hierarchy & Wacongne's Omitted-Tone Prediction Error
item.description: Electrophysiology of auditory expectation and hierarchical prediction error: Sutton et al. (1965) P300 discovery comparing identical clicks under certainty vs. uncertainty, Bekinschtein et al. (2009) local-global paradigm where a locally Deviant XXXXX/XXXXY sequence becomes the global rule, and Wacongne et al. (2011) brain responses to an omitted expected tone.

item.title: How a Cell Builds a Droplet in the Right Place — C. elegans P Granules, Brangwynne's Shear-Induced Dripping & FRAP Recovery, MEX-5 Gradient Dissolution & MEG-3 Scaffolding
item.description: Discovery of intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation: Hird et al. (1996) live GFP::PIE-1 imaging of C. elegans P granules, Brangwynne et al. (2009) proof of liquid wetting, fusion, ~second FRAP exchange, and spatial condensation/dissolution asymmetry, and Smith et al. (2016) & Folkmann et al. (2021) MEX-5 RNA competition and intrinsically disordered MEG-3 surface clusters.

item.title: How a Burst Leaves a Synapse Stronger — Bliss & Lømo's 1973 Perforant-Path LTP Controls, Collingridge's APV NMDA Blockade & Tsien's CA1-Restricted NR1 Knockout
item.description: Experimental dissection of hippocampal Long-Term Potentiation (LTP): Bliss & Lømo (1973) pathway-specific potentiation lasting hours in rabbit dentate gyrus, Collingridge, Kehl & McLennan (1983) selective NMDA antagonist APV blocking LTP induction while sparing baseline AMPA synaptic transmission, and Tsien, Huerta & Tonegawa (1996) postnatal CA1 NR1 knockout mice.

item.title: When the Lips Change the Sound You Hear — Sumby & Pollack's Speech-in-Noise Gain, McGurk & MacDonald's Ba/Ga→Da Fusion & Beauchamp's Superior Temporal Sulcus TMS Disruption
item.description: Multisensory speech integration and causal cortical testing: Sumby & Pollack (1954) audiovisual enhancement in noise across vocabulary set sizes, McGurk & MacDonald (1976) cross-modal syllable fusion where auditory /ba/ paired with lip-articulated /ga/ yields heard /da/, and Beauchamp, Nath & Pasalar (2010) fMRI-guided TMS over the superior temporal sulcus selectively reducing McGurk fusion while sparing congruent control syllables.

item.title: How a Sour Taste Starts — Huang's PKD2L1 Sour-Cell Ablation, Chang's Apical Proton Current, Tu's Otop1 Proton Channel Cloning & Teng/Zhang's Chorda Tympani Nerve Loss in Otop1-/- Mice
item.description: From cell-type ablation to the molecular proton sensor for sour taste: Huang et al. (2006) selective elimination of PKD2L1 taste cells erasing chorda tympani acid responses while sparing sweet, salty, bitter, and umami, Chang, Waters & Liman (2010) direct measurement of apical proton entry, Tu et al. (2018) discovery of the OTOP1 proton channel, and Teng et al. / Zhang et al. (2019) in vivo Otop1-/- requirement for sour nerve signaling.

item.title: How You Know Where Your Hand Is in the Dark — Goodwin's 100 Hz Tendon-Vibration Illusion, Ghez's Multi-Joint Reaching Without Proprioception, Woo's Piezo2 Spindles & Chesler's Human PIEZO2 Loss
item.description: From psychophysical illusions to the molecular mechanosensor of proprioception: Goodwin, McCloskey & Matthews (1972) tendon-vibration muscle-spindle illusions, Ghez et al. (1995) intersegmental dynamics defects in deafferented human reaching rescued partially by vision, Woo et al. (2015) conditional Piezo2 ablation silencing muscle-spindle Ia afferents, and Chesler et al. (2016) human PIEZO2 deficiency.

item.title: The Kidney After the Heat — Collecting-Duct AVP–V2R Cryo-EM (7DW9), AQP2 Ser256 Trafficking, Recurrent Rat Fructose Dehydration vs. Human Exercise Heat Crossovers
item.description: Separating physiological water conservation from tubular injury during heat stress and sweetened rehydration: human arginine vasopressin-V2R-Gs cryo-EM structure (PDB 7DW9) and PKA-driven AQP2 apical exocytosis, Chapman et al. (2020) 12-human heat-exercise soft-drink crossover, García-Arroyo et al. (2017) Wistar rat V1a/V2 conivaptan blockade, and Tourula et al. (2026) hypotonic vs. hypertonic sports drinks.

item.title: The Fructose That Locked Up Phosphate — Hereditary Fructose Intolerance, KHK Fructose-1-Phosphate Trapping vs. ALDOB A149P/A174D Crystal Structures, 31P-MRS Hepatic PME & KHK Inhibition
item.description: From infant post-weaning hypoglycemia, hypophosphatemia, hyperuricemia, and proximal renal Fanconi syndrome in Hereditary Fructose Intolerance to KHK-driven fructose-1-phosphate sequestration, human ALDOB A149P/A174D crystal structures, hepatic 31P-MRS phosphomonoester dynamics, and investigational ketohexokinase inhibition.

item.title: What an Eye Movement Can Tell Us About Dreaming — Aserinsky & Kleitman's 1953 EOG Awakenings, Dement's Duration Judgments, Foulkes's Definition Shift & Siclari's Posterior Hot Zone
item.description: From Aserinsky & Kleitman's (1953) discovery of Rapid Eye Movement sleep and Dement & Kleitman's (1957) 5-vs.-15-minute binary duration judgments to Foulkes's (1962) proof that NREM mental activity depends on definition thresholds and Siclari et al.'s (2017) posterior cortical low-frequency reduction predicting dream experience within both REM and NREM sleep.

item.title: A Sodium Channel for Pain and Smell — Cox's SCN9A (NaV1.7) Nonsense Variants, Patch-Clamp Loss of Current & Weiss's Olfactory Glomerular Synaptic Failure
item.description: How one voltage-gated sodium channel links nociception and olfaction: Cox et al. (2006) biallelic SCN9A (NaV1.7) truncations eliminating pain while sparing touch, and Weiss et al. (2011) dual recordings proving NaV1.7-null olfactory sensory neurons fire odor-evoked action potentials at the soma but fail to trigger synaptic transmission in the olfactory bulb glomerulus.

item.title: How Infants Tune In to Speech — Werker & Tees's 6-to-12-Month Head-Turn Narrowing, Maye's Bimodal vs. Unimodal Distributions, Kuhl's Live-vs.-Video Mandarin & Lytle's Peer Contingency
item.description: Perceptual narrowing in infant speech acquisition: Werker & Tees (1984) preservation of English contrasts alongside loss of non-native Hindi/Salish discrimination by 10–12 months, Maye, Werker & Gerken (2002) statistical bimodal vs. unimodal distribution reshaping, Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003) live vs. televised Mandarin tutors, and Lytle, Garcia-Sierra & Kuhl (2018) peer-paired contingent video.

item.title: How Light Sets the Body Clock — Rodless/Coneless Circadian Phase Shifts, Berson's Retrograde SCN Ganglion Cells, Melanopsin Knockout Rescue & Opn4Diphtheria Ablation
item.description: Discovery of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs): Freedman et al. (1999) intact circadian photoentrainment without rods and cones, Berson, Dunn & Takao (2002) intrinsic light responses in SCN-projecting ganglion cells after synaptic isolation, Hattar et al. (2003) triple-knockout loss of entrainment when rods, cones, and melanopsin are removed together, and Güler et al. (2008) ipRGC cell ablation.

item.title: How a Robin Reads the Tilt of a Magnetic Field — Wiltschko's 1972 Horizontal vs. Vertical Coil Flips, Ritz's Radio-Frequency Disruption & Xu's European Robin Cryptochrome 4
item.description: Biophysics of the avian inclination compass: Wiltschko & Wiltschko (1972) proof that European robins read magnetic field line dip angle (poleward vs. equatorward) rather than polarity, Ritz et al. (2004) diagnostic radio-frequency spin resonance disruption, and Xu et al. (2021) transient absorption spectroscopy of purified migratory European robin vs. non-migratory chicken/pigeon Cryptochrome 4.

item.title: Why an Aroma Can Seem to Come from Your Mouth — Rozin's Dual-Olfaction Juice Test, Dalton's Subthreshold Saccharin-Benzaldehyde Integration, Small's Retronasal fMRI & Blankenship's Optogenetics
item.description: Neurobiology of retronasal olfaction and flavor referral: Rozin (1982) dual-sense hypothesis, Dalton et al. (2000) subthreshold benzaldehyde + saccharin integration (28% lower threshold vs. null MSG control), Small et al. (2005) nasal-cannula fMRI showing route-dependent brain activation for identical vapor concentrations, and Blankenship et al. (2019) gustatory cortex requirement for rapid retronasal learning.

item.title: The Glucose That Couldn't Leave the Liver — Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia, ER G6PC1 His176 Phosphohistidine Catalysis vs. SLC37A4, Uncooked Cornstarch & DTX401 Gene Therapy
item.description: From acute fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis in glycogen storage disease type Ia to ER lumenal G6PC1 His176 phosphohistidine hydrolysis vs. SLC37A4 glucose-6-phosphate transport, Grefhorst's ChREBP/LXRalpha mouse blockade vs. human [6,6-2H2]glucose flux, uncooked cornstarch therapy, and AAV8 G6PC1 gene replacement.

item.title: The Pump at the Brain — Blood-Brain Barrier P-Glycoprotein (ABCB1) Efflux, Loperamide vs. Fentanyl CNS Exclusion, Cryo-EM ATPase Cycle & Drug-Drug Interactions
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into blood-brain barrier ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) efflux: why potent mu-opioid agonists like loperamide act peripherally unless P-gp is overwhelmed or inhibited, inward-to-outward cryo-EM peristaltic extrusion, and clinical transporter inhibition.

item.title: The Sugar That Stayed After the Milk Was Gone — Classic Galactosemia, GALT Ping-Pong His186 Catalysis (5IN3), Endogenous [1-13C]Galactose Production & Aldose Reductase
item.description: Why lifelong dietary galactose restriction saves neonates from acute hepatorenal crisis yet fails to prevent long-term speech and ovarian complications in classic galactosemia: human GALT double-displacement His186 uridylylation (PDB 5IN3), Berry et al. [1-13C]galactose isotope-dilution proof of ~1 g/day endogenous galactose synthesis, and aldose reductase galactitol reduction.

item.title: The Hormone That Heard Less Protein — Dietary Protein Restriction, Hepatocyte FGF21 Induction, Beta-Klotho 5VAQ Docking, FAP Cleavage & Intact vs. Total ELISA
item.description: Endocrine and structural dissection of human FGF21 induction during low-protein and sucrose feeding (Nicolaisen, Ramne, Laeger): C-terminal beta-Klotho docking (PDB 5VAQ), fibroblast activation protein (FAP) Pro171 cleavage separating intact bioactive FGF21 from total immunoreactive FGF21, and central Klb macronutrient preference circuits.

item.title: How the Nose Builds an Odor Code — Buck & Axel's Olfactory Receptor Family, Zhao's Adenoviral I7 Pairing, Malnic's Combinatorial Code & Bozza's Bulb Glomeruli
item.description: Molecular logic of combinatorial olfaction: Buck & Axel (1991) cloning of the odorant receptor superfamily, Zhao et al. (1998) functional pairing of receptor I7 with octanal, Malnic et al. (1999) single-neuron calcium imaging + RT-PCR showing concentration-dependent recruitment (2 to 5 to 8 receptors for bromooctanoic acid), and Bozza et al. (2004) in vivo glomerular synapto-pHluorin maps.

item.title: The Mirror-Image Test for an Opioid Receptor — Goldstein's Stereospecificity, Pert & Snyder's [3H]Naloxone Levorphanol vs. Dextrorphan Assay & Enkephalin Discovery
item.description: Biochemical proof of brain opioid receptors: Goldstein et al. (1971) enantiomeric competition concept, Pert & Snyder (1973) [3H]naloxone vacuum-filtration assay showing stereospecific displacement by (-)-levorphanol but not (+)-dextrorphan, Hughes et al. (1975) discovery of endogenous pentapeptides Met- and Leu-enkephalin, and 1992 delta-receptor cloning.

item.title: What the Colon Sends Back — Inulin Fermentation, Eudragit Colon-Targeted [1-13C]SCFAs, Systemic Availability (36% Acetate, 9% Propionate, 2% Butyrate) & FFAR2 8J24
item.description: Atomic and clinical tracing of colonic short-chain fatty acids (Boets et al. 2015, 2017; Bloemen et al. 2009): Bacteroides ovatus inulin cleavage, Roseburia/Faecalibacterium acetate-to-butyrate cross-feeding, Eudragit S100 colon-targeted [1-13C]SCFA capsules with IV [2H]SCFA clearance calibration (36% acetate, 9.2% propionate, 2.4% butyrate systemic availability), and human FFAR2 cryo-EM (PDB 8J24).

item.title: The First Calories Back — Refeeding Syndrome, Insulin-Driven Phosphate/Potassium Shifts, PDH E1 ThDP Geometry (1NI4) & Doig ICU Trial
item.description: From starvation to refeeding syndrome in the ICU: insulin-stimulated Na+/K+-ATPase potassium uptake and intracellular phosphate trapping, human pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 thiamine diphosphate (ThDP) active-site geometry (PDB 1NI4), whole-blood ThDP LC-MS/MS assays, diaphragmatic weakness in hypophosphatemia (Aubier 1985), and the Doig et al. (2015) caloric restriction trial.

item.title: The Leucine That Wouldn’t Clear — Maple Syrup Urine Disease, BCKDH E1 Phosphorylation (1DTW/1OLS), Isobaric LC-MS/MS Alloisoleucine & Liver Transplant Flux
item.description: Biochemical and analytical dissection of Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD) decompensation: human BCKDH E1 alpha-ketoacid decarboxylation and BCKDK Ser292 phosphorylation (PDB 1DTW/1OLS/4H7Q), chromatographic separation of isobaric leucine, isoleucine, alloisoleucine, and hydroxyproline at m/z 132->86, LAT1 blood-brain barrier competition, IV BCAA-free rescue, and liver transplantation.

item.title: When GABA Pulls Voltage the Other Way — KCC2 Chloride Extrusion, Gramicidin-Perforated Patch Anion Reversal & Microglial BDNF in Neuropathic Pain
item.description: Ionic basis of GABAergic polarity switches: Rivera et al. (1999) KCC2 antisense knockdown in hippocampal neurons, Coull et al. (2003, 2005) gramicidin-perforated patch recordings in spinal lamina I after nerve injury (-72.6 mV to -49.0 mV) driven by microglial BDNF-TrkB signaling, and depolarizing shunting conductance.

item.title: How a Shark Finds a Fish Under Sand — Murray's Ampullae of Lorenzini Recordings, Kalmijn's Agar-Chamber & Dipole Strikes & Sawfish Electrosense
item.description: Experimental proof of passive electroreception in elasmobranchs: Murray (1962) ampullae of Lorenzini nerve recordings, Kalmijn (1971) catshark and skate strikes at agar-screened live plaice vs. polyethylene insulation vs. artificial bioelectric dipoles, and Wueringer et al. (2012) sawfish rostral electrosense.

item.title: A Chemical Signal Comes in Packets — Fatt & Katz Miniature Endplate Potentials, Del Castillo & Katz Poisson Quantal Failures & Heuser-Reese Quick-Freeze Exocytosis
item.description: Statistical and ultrastructural proof of quantal synaptic transmission: Fatt & Katz (1952) spontaneous miniature endplate potentials, del Castillo & Katz (1954) independent quantal content estimates (0.57 by amplitude ratio vs. 0.56 by Poisson failure fraction), and Heuser & Reese (1979) 3–5 ms quick-freeze electron microscopy.

item.title: Why a Chili Pepper Feels Hot — Caterina & Julius's TRPV1 Expression-Cloning Screen, Thermal Activation, Knockout Hyperalgesia & Chicken-Rat Chimeras
item.description: Discovery and dissection of polymodal nociception via TRPV1: Caterina et al. (1997) Fura-2 expression cloning from dorsal root ganglia, physical heat (>43°C) gating of the capsaicin receptor, Caterina et al. (2000) TRPV1-/- loss of inflammatory thermal hyperalgesia, and Jordt & Julius (2002) separation of capsaicin and thermal gating in avian-mammalian chimeras.

item.title: A Message That Traveled in Blood — Bayliss & Starling's 1902 Denervated Jejunal Loop, the Discovery of Secretin, Peptide Sequencing & Receptor Cloning
item.description: Birth of endocrinology and humoral signaling: Bayliss & Starling (1902) surgically denervated jejunal loop acid challenge, intravenous jejunal vs. ileal extract controls Separating pancreatic secretion from vasodepression, Mutt et al. (1970) porcine secretin purification, and Ishihara et al. (1991) secretin receptor cAMP signaling.

item.title: How the Ear Turns Up Its Own Volume — Brownell's Outer Hair Cell Electromotility, Zheng's Prestin Discovery & Dallos's Stiffness-Preserving Knock-In
item.description: Biophysics of the cochlear amplifier: Brownell et al. (1985) voltage-driven length changes in guinea-pig outer hair cells, Zheng et al. (2000) subtractive cloning of prestin (SLC26A5), Liberman et al. (2002) 40–60 dB threshold shift in prestin-/- mice, and Dallos et al. (2008) 499-prestin knock-in separating active motor force from passive axial stiffness.

item.title: One Ångström When the Artery Opens — Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion, Succinate Accumulation, Complex I Reverse Electron Transport & Infarct Salvage
item.description: Atomic and clinical timeline of the first minutes after coronary artery reperfusion: Jennings & Reimer's (1960/1977) canine wavefront of necrosis, coronary-sinus succinate release, Complex I flavin site reverse electron transport (RET) superoxide burst upon reoxygenation, and why ischemic postconditioning failed to reduce clinical STEMI endpoints.

item.title: The Carbon in the Next Breath — [U-13C6]Fructose Meal Oxidation, KHK-A 2HW1 Active Site, GC-C-IRMS Plasma Glucose & 7T Hepatic Deuterium Imaging
item.description: Stable-isotope tracing of ingested [U-13C6]fructose in humans (Theytaz et al. 2014): GLUT5 uptake, ketohexokinase KHK-A vs. KHK-C phosphorylation (PDB 2HW1), aldolase B cleavage, GC-C-IRMS 13C-glucose and breath 13CO2 recovery, paired with 7-Tesla hepatic deuterium metabolic imaging (Brunasso et al. 2026).

item.title: How a Bat Measures the Dark — Pierce & Griffin's Ultrasonic Detector, Galambos's Obstacle Course & Simmons's Electronic Echo-Delay Target Illusion
item.description: Experimental discovery of bat echolocation: Pierce & Griffin (1938) ultrasonic heterodyne detector, Griffin & Galambos (1941) reversible sight vs. hearing vs. vocalization blocks, terminal buzz pursuit (1960), and Kick & Simmons (1984) electronic delay-line phantom targets.

item.title: How Chloroplasts Made ATP in the Dark — Mitchell's Chemiosmotic Hypothesis, Jagendorf & Uribe's Acid-Bath pH Jump & Racker-Stoeckenius Chimeric Vesicles
item.description: Decisive experimental tests of chemiosmotic coupling: Mitchell (1961), Jagendorf & Uribe (1966) spinach thylakoid acid-bath pH jump (141 vs. 12 nmol ATP/mg chlorophyll in darkness), and Racker & Stoeckenius (1974) halobacterial bacteriorhodopsin + bovine mitochondrial ATP synthase proteoliposomes.

item.title: When One Eye Takes the Lead — Wiesel & Hubel's Monocular vs. Binocular Deprivation, Critical Period Timing & Pizzorusso's Perineuronal Net Chondroitinase
item.description: Synaptic competition and critical period closure in visual cortex: Wiesel & Hubel (1963–1970) why monocular suture shifts cortical drive (1/84 cells) while binocular suture preserves responsiveness, and Pizzorusso et al. (2002) extracellular matrix chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan digestion in adult rats.

item.title: The Butterfly That Steers by a Clock — Monarch Phase-Shifted Flight Simulators, Antennal Circadian Clocks & Conflicting Black-vs.-Clear Enamel Inputs
item.description: Neuroethology of the monarch butterfly time-compensated sun compass: Mouritsen & Frost (2002) ±6h photoperiod shifts (225° vs. 136° vs. 335°), Merlin et al. (2009) antennal light-entrained circadian oscillators, and Guerra et al. (2012) rescue of group orientation by amputating a desynchronized black-painted antenna.

item.title: One Ångström Through the Splenic Gate — Red Cell Interendothelial Slits, PIEZO1 Hereditary Xerocytosis (8YEZ/8YFG), Gardos KCNN4 & Ektacytometry
item.description: Squeezing a human erythrocyte through a sub-micron splenic interendothelial slit: PIEZO1 mechanosensitive dome flattening and MDFIC-bound slowed inactivation (PDB 8YEZ/8YFG, 6.1 ms vs. 17.4 ms), Ca2+-activated Gardos (KCNN4) potassium/water efflux, osmotic gradient ektacytometry shifts, and why splenectomy triggers portal/thrombotic catastrophe in PIEZO1 hereditary xerocytosis.

item.title: One Ångström Under the Mucus — Human Airway Axonemal Dynein (PDB 8J07), Periciliary Brush Exclusion, DNAH5 Splice Defects & Nasal Nitric Oxide
item.description: Atomic-to-clinical journey through mucociliary clearance and Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD): human airway doublet microtubule structure (Walton et al. 2023, PDB 8J07), periciliary brush osmotic exclusion (Button et al. 2012), nasal nitric oxide chemiluminescence, and DNAH5 intronic splice-site RT-PCR.

item.title: Three Roads to Liver Fat — Chylomicron NEFA Spillover, Multi-Tracer Liver Biopsies, Human FASN 9MJ9 & Beverage De Novo Lipogenesis
item.description: Quantitative isotope dissection of hepatic triacylglycerol sources across three human studies: Piché et al. (2018) chylomicron-derived [U-13C]palmitate spillover, Donnelly et al. (2005) 4-day triple-tracer liver biopsies (59% NEFA, 26% DNL, 15% dietary within accounted fraction), human FASN cryo-EM (PDB 9MJ9), and Geidl-Flueck et al. (2021) sugar-sweetened beverage VLDL-palmitate secretion.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: A Flash in the Dark — Hecht-Shlaer-Pirenne Thresholds (1942), Baylor Single-Rod Suction Pipettes (1979) & cGMP Gating
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 1: from Hecht, Shlaer & Pirenne's (1942) 5-14 photon human psychophysical threshold to Baylor, Lamb & Yau's (1979) 1 pA single-photon suction-pipette recordings in toad rod outer segments and Fesenko et al.'s (1985) inside-out patch cGMP gating proof.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: What Does a Nerve Impulse Cost? — Squid Giant Axon Voltage Clamp (1952) vs. Mammalian Mossy-Fiber Na+ Load (2009)
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 2: separating net voltage change from opposing Na+ and K+ fluxes—from Hodgkin & Huxley's (1952) squid axon model to Alle, Roth & Geiger's (2009) action-potential clamp in rat hippocampal mossy fibers showing 1.3x capacitive minimum Na+ entry.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: How a Touch Becomes a Current — Chick Muscle Stretch Channels (1984), Piezo1/2 RNAi Screen (2010) & Bilayer Reconstitution
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 3: how Guharay & Sachs (1984), Coste et al. (2010, 2012), Ranade et al. (2014), and Syeda et al. (2016) proved that Piezo1 and Piezo2 are the bona fide pore-forming mechanosensitive ion channels underlying vertebrate gentle touch.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: Can an Active Neuron Use Glucose Directly? — Astrocyte-Neuron Lactate Shuttle (1994) vs. Peredox NADH Imaging (2017)
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 4: testing the Astrocyte-Neuron Lactate Shuttle (Pellerin & Magistretti 1994) with single-neuron Peredox NADH/NAD+ fluorescence lifetime imaging and MCT1/2 blockade in hippocampal slices and awake mice (Diaz-Garcia et al. 2017).

item.title: One Ångström from a Dividing Cell — Paclitaxel in the β-Tubulin Taxane Pocket (1JFF), Cremophor Anaphylaxis & Mitotic Spindle Fate
item.description: Atomic-scale journey into the luminal beta-tubulin taxane pocket (PDB 1JFF): distinguishing Cremophor EL complement-mediated infusion anaphylaxis from delayed neutropenia, M-loop lateral protofilament stabilization, and multipolar mitotic spindle catastrophe in human tumors.

item.title: One Ångström Across the Gut Barrier — Enteric Translocation, TLR4–MD-2 Lipid A Dimerization (3FXI), Microvascular Shunting & Septic Shock
item.description: From an injured intestinal barrier and mesenteric lymph node cultures (Deitch 1989) to the crystal structure of human TLR4-MD-2 bound to E. coli Ra LPS (PDB 3FXI), sublingual microvascular shunting (De Backer 2002), endothelial glycocalyx shedding, and why eritoran MD-2 blockade failed in the Phase III ACCESS sepsis trial.

item.title: One Ångström Riding the Flagellum — Sperm Capacitation, CatSper Pore Architecture (7EEB), Whole-Cell Patch Clamp & Hyperactivated Beat
item.description: Atomic and electrophysiological journey along the principal piece of a sperm flagellum: mouse CatSperosome cryo-EM architecture (PDB 7EEB) vs. human cytoplasmic-droplet whole-cell patch-clamp recordings (Lishko/Strunker 2011; Mansell 2014), the 2016 ABHD2 hypothesis vs. 2026 selective inhibitor tests, and CATSPER-deficient IVF failure rescued by ICSI.
